newsitem.title: USA: U.S. concern at Turkish warship arrival in Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. concern at Turkish warship arrival in Cyprus.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it was concerned by reports of the arrival of Turkish warships in northern Cyprus and was seeking an explanation from Ankara.

The Cyprus government said on Tuesday it would protest to the United Nations against the arrival of six Turkish warships and three submarines for naval exercises off northern Cyprus, where Turkish troops have been stationed since 1974.

"We're very concerned about the reports of the movement of Turkish naval vessels," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said. "The United States, frankly, does not know the reasons behind these reported naval manoeuvres."
"We are seeking an explanation from the Turkish government," Burns told a news briefing.

He said it was very important that no party should take "unilateral measures" that could disrupt United Nations- sponsored peace talks between Greek and Turkish Cypriot leaders slated to begin near New York July 9.
The Turkish Cypriots have set up a mini-state in the northern third of Cyprus that is recognised only by Ankara.
The United States recently appointed Richard Holbrooke, negotiator of the Bosnia peace accord in 1995, as special envoy for Cyprus in a bid to foster a settlement.
